case_name: O.P. Bhandari v Indian Tourism Development Corporation Limited
respondent:
Indian Tourism Development Corporation Limited
Supreme Court of India

26 September 1986
Civil Appeal No. 1969 of 1986 From the Judgment and order dated 26.9.1984 of the Delhi High Court in Civil Writ Petition No. 2329 of 1984.
The Judgment was delivered by: Thakkar, J.
1. A CAT scan of this appeal reveals three problems, viz:
I. Whether a rule or regulation framed by a public sector undertaking which is an authority under the control of Government of India and is a 'State' within the parameters of Art. 12 of the Constitution of India empowering the employer to terminate the services of an employee by giving notice of the prescribed period or payment of salary for the notice period in lieu of such notice is constitutional?
II. If it is unconstitutional, whether the employee whose services are terminated under the said rule or regulation is always and invariably entitled to reinstatement? Whether option to pay compensation in lieu of reinstatement can be given to the emp
facts: The respondent Corporation (I.T.D.C.) is 'State' within the parameters of Art. 12 of the Constitution of India it being an instrumentality of the State as per the law enunciated by this Court in Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Limited & Anr. v. Brojo Nath Ganguly and Anr. 1986 Indlaw SC 645 and Central Inland Water Transport Corporation Limited & Anr. v. Taran Kanti Sengupta & Anr., [1986] 3 S.C.C. 156 1986 Indlaw SC 645.
Appellant was an employee of the Respondent Corporation holding the post of Manager of Hotel Ranjit, New Delhi, at the material time when his services were terminated by the impugned order.

Services of the Appellant were terminated in exercise of powers under Rule 31 (v) of the ITDC Conduct Discipline and Appeal Rules 1978, (ITDC rules) by giving pay for 3 months in lieu of 3 months' notice, under the said rule.
issues: Whether a rule or regulation framed by a public sector undertaking which is an authority under the control of Government of India and is a 'State' within the parameters of Art. 12 of the Constitution of India empowering the employer to terminate the services of an employee by giving notice of the prescribed period or payment of salary for the notice period in lieu of such notice is constitutional?
If it is unconstitutional, whether the employee whose services are terminated under the said rule or regulation is always and invariably entitled to reinstatement?
Whether option to pay compensation in lieu of reinstatement can be given to the employer in fit cases?
What would be the appropriate amount to be reasonably awarded in lieu of reinstatement?
petitioner_arguments: The power may be exercised even on the unarticulated ground that the former belongs to the same religious faith or is the disciple of the same religious teacher or holds opinions congenial to him.

Such a rule is capable of robbing an employee of his dignity, and making him a supine person whose destiny is at the mercy of the concerned authority (whom he must humour) notwithstanding the Constitutional guarantee enshrined in Arts. 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India.
court_reasoning: The impugned regulation is extremely wide in its coverage in the sense that it embraces the 'blue collar' workmen, the 'white collar' employees, as also the 'gold collar' (managerial cadre) employees of the Undertaking.
In so far as the 'blue collar' and 'white collar' employees are concerned, the quashing does not pose any problem.
In so far as the 'gold collar' (managerial cadre) employees are concerned, the consequence of quashing of the regulation calls for some reflection.
holding: The rule in question must be held to be unconstitutional and void.

Rule 31(v) of the aforesaid ITDC rules which provides for termination of the services of the employees of the respondent corporation simply by giving 90 days' notice or by payment of salary for the notice period in lieu of such notice, deserves to be quashed.
